scope: Research-only eight source literature descriptions, NOT Hays specimen signoffs
sources: Illustrated Flora of North Central Texas 1999 (user Library PDF); explicit historical concept markers
Hagenbuch and Lemke 2015 Texas Hill Country grass key for regional name context
Kew POWO/GrassBase and Flora of North America treatments for present accepted species and details
Previously saved Hays 58 iNaturalist source-photo visual QA, reused not re-inspected
not_authorized: No iNaturalist IDs promoted to botanically verified

taxa.regional_flora_scope: Direct 1999 Flora species and brome key

source_described_characters.description: Winter annual 10–70 cm in flower; green growth may start late in fall
Strongly flattened spikelet; glumes and lemmas sharply keeled
Lower lemma about 2.5–3.2 mm wide from keel to margin
Lemmas awnless or with short awn about 1–3 mm
Minute lemma-apex teeth around 0.1–0.3 mm
Leaf sheath with spreading pilose hairs; spikelets hairless

taxa.prior_Hays_photo_evidence: Open to somewhat loose grass panicle with flattened-looking elongated hanging spikelets; green grassy stand and culm close-ups visible.
taxa.unresolved_from_prior_photos: Sharp keel, exact awn lengths, lemma teeth/veins and collar/ligule not resolved; cannot rule out lookalike Bromus from gross view alone.
taxa.lookalikes: Bromus hordeaceus, B. japonicus, B. secalinus
taxa.next_same_specimen_evidence: A complete mature spikelet, keeled glumes/lemmas and tooth/awn measurements, sheath hairs and collar on the same Hays specimen.

taxa.regional_flora_scope: Rechecked 2026-11-12: vegetative primary Hagenbuch & Lemke (2015), p. 49; reproductive primary Diggs et al. (1999), printed pp. 1272, 1274. Earlier FNA/GrassBase reproductive details retained as supplementary, not newly reverified. No new specimen or image review; all admission holds remain.

source_described_characters.description: Tufted perennial without rhizomes or stolons in the Hill Country account; hair-fringe ligule to 1 mm, smooth sheath surfaces with hairy margins, blades flat or inward-rolled. Range planting context is a separate Flora observation, not species proof.
source_described_characters.source: Hagenbuch & Lemke (2015), p. 49, https://www.phytoneuron.net/2015Phytoneuron/04PhytoN-HillCountryGrasses.pdf#page=49; Diggs et al. (1999), printed pp. 1272, 1274
source_described_characters.needed_view: connected crown, opened inner ligule with scale, sheath surface and margin on the same plant

source_described_characters.description: Broad, strongly compressed and showy, around 3–10 mm wide
source_described_characters.source: Diggs et al. (1999), printed p. 1272 (account continues p. 1274)

source_described_characters.description: Lemma has conspicuous keel
source_described_characters.source: Diggs et al. (1999), printed p. 1272 (account continues p. 1274)

source_described_characters.description: Multiflowered spikelet, roughly 4–22 florets in FNA
Mature spikelet may detach whole below the glumes
Palea keels broadly winged, a crucial tiny structural character

taxa.prior_Hays_photo_evidence: Tufted dry to green bunchgrass; rather large flattened light tan spikelets on branched stems, with some hand-scaled seedhead views.
taxa.unresolved_from_prior_photos: Detached florets, glume and lemma veins/hair characters not resolved; introduced planting versus established escape not confirmed.
taxa.lookalikes: Eragrostis intermedia, E. spectabilis, E. curvula
taxa.next_same_specimen_evidence: Ripe flattened spikelet on mm scale, isolated lemma and winged palea, true ligule, basal crown and evidence of unplanted reproduction. The broad tuft and hair-fringe observations could map to habit=tuft and ligule=hairs only after specimen review; they also fit other lovegrasses and cannot alone establish identity. Do not assign head=flat_oats from flattened spikelets: that option requires dangling oat-like attachment, not just lateral compression. The short regional account does not establish that architecture.

taxa.regional_flora_scope: 1999 Flora treats multiflorum as subspecies, while modern Kew recognizes two species

source_described_characters.description: Single upright two-ranked axis bearing solitary edge-on spikelets
Glume shorter than total spikelet, often 5–10 mm in old regional key
Typical L. perenne lemma awnless; hybrids and rare variants complicate simple splits
Shorter, relatively rounded auricles compared with older multiflorum concept
Typically 4–14 fertile florets per spikelet in Kew GrassBase account

taxa.prior_Hays_photo_evidence: Unbranched ryegrass-like flowering spikes with spikelets edge-on along central rachis; a basal bunch and habitat views.
taxa.unresolved_from_prior_photos: Awn presence/absence, floret and glume dimensions and discrimination from L. multiflorum or their hybrid not confidently resolved.
taxa.next_same_specimen_evidence: Same-plant auricles, 3 mature spikelets showing glume/lemma/awn/floret count, and seeded turf versus wild context.

taxa.regional_flora_treatment: Bothriochloa laguroides subsp. torreyana (broad older concept)
taxa.regional_flora_scope: Historical 1999 Flora LUMPS longipaniculata into torreyana; only group-level descriptions usable

source_described_characters.description: Sessile/pedicelled pairs and grooved internodes characterize Bothriochloa genus
Whitened or silvery branched seedhead belongs to broad historical silver-bluestem group
Historic B. laguroides group key describes short sessile spikelets below 4.5 mm and awns usually 18 mm or shorter, NOT a modern longipaniculata diagnosis
Old torreyana treatment notes stems 50–130 cm and exserted flowering panicles; NOT species-exclusive

taxa.prior_Hays_photo_evidence: Silvery narrow feathery panicle and upright grass culms; basal grassy tuft shown. Multiple close flowering head views are present.
taxa.unresolved_from_prior_photos: No glume macro adequate to check narrow shiny green vs broad dull glumes; reliable panicle-length measurement unavailable; can't separate from B. torreyana on these views.
taxa.next_same_specimen_evidence: Find true species-rank modern differential; compare same-scale panicle and detached sessile glumes between independently verified longipaniculata and torreyana.

taxa.regional_flora_treatment: No direct modern species treatment in 1999 Flora
taxa.regional_flora_scope: Kew POWO FTEA/GrassBase description supplies species concepts; Flora genus key only

source_described_characters.description: Tufted or shortly rhizomatous perennial with erect stems
Numerous short racemes, around 2–5 cm, on a central branching axis
Sessile fertile and usually smaller pedicelled sterile spikelets occur as pairs
Rachis internodes and pedicels flattened with a median translucent groove/line
Sessile spikelets about 3–4 mm with usually hairy lower glume, sometimes pitted but pit variable
Geniculate awn often 10–25 mm across Kew source treatments

taxa.prior_Hays_photo_evidence: Several fingerlike burgundy-purple racemes and paired spikelets/awn-like projections; strong magnification at hand scale and an exposed collar area in one observation.
taxa.unresolved_from_prior_photos: Distinctive paired-spikelet glumes, exact lemma awns, node collar anatomy and distinction from Dichanthium or KR bluestem unresolved.
taxa.lookalikes: Bothriochloa ischaemum, Dichanthium aristatum, D. annulatum
taxa.next_same_specimen_evidence: Measure a matched sessile/pedicelled pair, glume pit/hair pattern, rachis median line, lemma awn, collar and root crown.

taxa.regional_flora_treatment: 1999 Flora treats D. annulatum, not aristatum itself
taxa.regional_flora_scope: 1999 Flora Dichanthium page is comparison-only; Kew POWO/PlantNET provide species treatment

source_described_characters.description: Perennial with ascending stems about 20–100 cm
One to six near-digitate racemes, mostly about 2–8 cm
Raceme base can be bare but notably hairy; bare bases alone mislead a Bothriochloa separation
Pedicel lacks Bothriochloa-type transparent median line
Sessile fertile spikelet about 2–5 mm and lower glume often hairy below middle
Fertile lemma often carries twisted/bent awn roughly 10–20 mm

taxa.prior_Hays_photo_evidence: Two to several reddish spreading racemes with awns, some extremely close flowering axis views, a ligule/collar view and bunchgrass basal shoots.
taxa.unresolved_from_prior_photos: The distinguishing pair of sessile and pedicellate spikelets, nerve and awn anatomy versus B. bladhii not measured; species confirmation pending.
taxa.lookalikes: Bothriochloa bladhii, Dichanthium annulatum, B. ischaemum
taxa.next_same_specimen_evidence: Examine pubescent raceme base, spikelet pairs, transparent median-line absence, glume hairs and bent awn against verified comparators.

taxa.regional_flora_scope: Direct old infraspecific Flora treatment, modern Kew separate species

source_described_characters.description: Single two-ranked ryegrass spike with alternating spikelets
Typically awned lemmas, often about 5–10 mm, though exceptions occur
Longer, more pointed auricles in regional subsp. multiflorum treatment
Membranous ligule commonly around 1–2 mm
Often about 5–15 florets per spikelet in Kew GrassBase account
Rachis can be distinctly scabrous, a supporting comparison with smoother perenne

taxa.prior_Hays_photo_evidence: Flattened spikelets alternating along an unbranched ryegrass rachis, some clearly awned in close-up; roadside or grassy habitats.
taxa.unresolved_from_prior_photos: Not all specimens' awns, glume characters or hybrid status clear; L. perenne / L. × boucheanum lookalikes possible.
taxa.lookalikes: Lolium perenne, Lolium × boucheanum, L. temulentum
taxa.next_same_specimen_evidence: Same plant leaf auricles and ligule, 3 mature spikelets showing awn, glumes, florets and rachis texture, with seeding/escape context.

taxa.regional_flora_treatment: Not covered as separate species in 1999 Flora
taxa.regional_flora_scope: Kew accepted name and global range only; NO defensible Hays species-level diagnostic description yet

source_described_characters.description: Accepted Bromus species at Kew; taxon acceptance alone says nothing about Hays occurrence
Known native range in central/southwestern Argentina; Kew introduced regions presently listed outside Texas
Kew records annual or perennial growth; this is not itself diagnostic

taxa.prior_Hays_photo_evidence: Some long open or somewhat contracted brome-like panicles and elongated spikelets photographed in lawns and disturbed grassland.
taxa.unresolved_from_prior_photos: Photographs vary markedly in spikelet/panicle habit; diagnostic glume and lemma metrics not shown. One observation has recorded ID disagreement. Current global literature does not clearly support a naturally established Hays population.
taxa.lookalikes: Bromus catharticus and other similar rescue bromes
taxa.next_same_specimen_evidence: Obtain independent Hays voucher expert ID and a modern Bromus brevis species key, then measure glumes, lemmas, awns and florets side-by-side with local B. catharticus.
